sections.content:
47,025 people

were counted on the census as "artists" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Artists create artistic works using appropriate techniques, materials and media; design artwork and illustrations; and restore damaged pieces of art.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "artists" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "artists", 11.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "artists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "artists" included:

  • other skilled trades
  • chartered surveyors
  • authors, writers and translators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "artists" there were more women than men (60.8% compared with 39.2%).

This means "artists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 39.2% and women made up 60.8% of "artists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "artists" included:

  • head teachers and principals
  • human resource managers and directors
  • bed and breakfast and guest house owners and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "artists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "artists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "artists", 18.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (50.9% compared with 49.1%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (86.3%) than an employee (13.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
